app.engagement_scope: Owner-authorized black-box exploration plus non-destructive active validation using two owner-supplied test accounts: member@example.com (Member, Organization A) and admin@example.com (Admin, Organization B). No Admin credentials for Organization A were provided/used. No destructive actions performed. No ID-enumeration attempted against any tenant other than Organization A and Organization B.
app.notes: Anonymized example model derived from a real two-tenant document-collaboration SaaS engagement. Organization/user names, emails, and the target URL have been replaced with generic placeholders; all structural findings, statuses, and evidence descriptions are preserved as originally recorded.

actors.name: Anonymous visitor
actors.description: Unauthenticated user hitting the app before login

actors.name: Member
actors.description: Authenticated user with role Member, scoped to exactly one organization observed (Organization A)
actors.evidence: Account member@example.com logged in showing role badge 'Member' within organization 'Organization A'

actors.name: Admin
actors.description: Authenticated user with role Admin, scoped to exactly one organization observed (Organization B); gains Team/Invitations management on top of Member-level capabilities
actors.evidence: Account admin@example.com logged in showing role badge 'Admin' within organization 'Organization B', with additional 'Invitations' nav item and 'Invite Member' button not present for the Member account
actors.evidence_source: Sidebar UI, dashboard and Team page, Round 2

tenants.name: Organization A
tenants.description: Organization tenant containing the Member test account and its documents
tenants.evidence: Dashboard and sidebar consistently labeled 'Organization A' for member@example.com

tenants.name: Organization B
tenants.description: Organization tenant containing the Admin test account, 1 member, and 3 documents
tenants.evidence: Dashboard and sidebar consistently labeled 'Organization B' for admin@example.com; dashboard reported MEMBERS 1, DOCUMENTS 3

resources.name: Document
resources.description: Core content object: title, body/content, created_by (owner), organization, created_date. Routes: /documents/<id> (view), /documents/<id>/edit (edit).
resources.evidence: Documents list and individual document pages observed in both tenants

resources.name: Team member / roster entry
resources.description: A user's membership record within an organization (name, email, role), shown on the Team page
resources.evidence: Team page listed only the current org's members in both tenants

resources.name: Invitation
resources.description: Pending invite to join an organization with a specified role (Member or Admin), managed via /invitations and the Team page's 'Invite Member' modal
resources.evidence: Invite Member modal with Email + Role (Member/Admin) fields and 'Send invitation' button was reachable for the Admin account; no invitation was actually sent

relationships.description: Document.created_by -> User; each document has exactly one owning author
relationships.evidence: Document view pages show a 'Created by' field naming a specific user

relationships.description: User belongs to an organization; both test accounts showed membership in exactly one organization each via the org switcher, which displayed only that org plus 'Sign out' with no option to switch to another org
relationships.evidence: Org switcher dropdown for both accounts showed only the current org's identity and a Sign out action, no list of other orgs

relationships.description: Documents are scoped to exactly one organization/tenant
relationships.evidence: Organization B Admin could not read or write Organization A's document by direct ID
relationships.evidence_source: Round 2 active validation, see validation_results VR1 and VR2

relationships.description: Team roster is scoped to exactly one organization/tenant
relationships.evidence: Organization B Admin's /team page showed only Organization B's own 1 member; this was not an active attempt to directly fetch Organization A's roster, so it is observational support rather than a confirmed isolation test.
relationships.evidence_source: Round 2 active validation, see validation_results VR3

conditions: any author, including documents not owned by the actor
authorization_rules.evidence: Member account (member_user) viewed Admin-authored document 'Org A Financial Report' in its own org without restriction
Member account successfully created 'test-doc-created-by-member' via the New Document flow

conditions: actor is the document's author (same org, own document)
authorization_rules.evidence: Member account edited and saved its own document 'test-doc-created-by-member' successfully

conditions: actor is NOT the document's author
accessed directly via /documents/<id>/edit, bypassing the UI which hides the edit affordance
authorization_rules.evidence: Member account attempted to edit Admin-authored 'Org A Financial Report' directly by URL; server rejected the save with 'You can only edit your own documents'; re-fetch of the document afterward confirmed content was unchanged
authorization_rules.evidence_source: Round 1 active validation, direct edit attempt on /documents/<org-a-doc-id>/edit plus re-fetch of /documents/<org-a-doc-id>

authorization_rules.evidence: No delete control (button, menu item, or route) was found anywhere in the UI for the Member role, on own or others' documents
authorization_rules.evidence_source: Round 1, exhaustive UI review of document view and edit pages

authorization_rules.evidence: No delete control (button, menu item, or route) was found anywhere in the UI for the Admin role either, including on the Admin's own documents
authorization_rules.evidence_source: Round 2, exhaustive UI review of document view and edit pages under Organization B

conditions: document belongs to a different organization/tenant than the actor's own
authorization_rules.evidence: Organization B Admin account requested Organization A's 'Org A Financial Report' by direct ID via /documents/<org-a-doc-id>; response was 'Document not found', identical to a genuinely nonexistent ID, with no data or existence leakage

conditions: document belongs to a different organization/tenant than the actor's own
authorization_rules.evidence: Organization B Admin loaded /documents/<org-a-doc-id>/edit; the editor rendered an empty 'Untitled document' form rather than the real Organization A content (no data exposure), and submitting 'Save changes' produced no persisted change: no phantom document appeared in Organization B's list, and re-fetching the Organization A document afterward showed its original content ('ORG-A-DOC-001') unchanged

conditions: roster belongs to a different organization/tenant than the actor's own
authorization_rules.evidence: Organization B Admin's own /team page listed only Organization B's 1 member. This was passive observation of the Organization B view, not an active attempt to directly request Organization A's roster by ID or endpoint, so it does not confirm a deny outcome for a genuine cross-tenant roster-read attempt.

conditions: actor role is Member, not Admin
accessed directly via /invitations, bypassing the UI which hides the Invitations nav item for Members
authorization_rules.evidence: Member account (member_user) navigated directly to /invitations; server-rendered block: 'Admins only - Only organization admins can manage invitations', not merely a hidden UI element

conditions: role to assign is Member or Admin
authorization_rules.evidence: Admin account opened the 'Invite member' modal showing Email and Role (Member/Admin) fields and a 'Send invitation' button; the modal rendering and field presence were directly observed, but the invitation was never actually submitted, so the application was never seen exercising the underlying invite-creation path end-to-end.
authorization_rules.evidence_source: Round 2, /team page Invite Member modal (not submitted)

conditions: actor is NOT the document's author
authorization_rules.evidence: Organization B (the only tenant with an Admin test account) had just 1 member, so no same-organization document authored by a different user existed to test whether Admin can edit another member's document within the same tenant
authorization_rules.evidence_source: Round 2, Organization B dashboard reporting MEMBERS: 1

security_invariants.statement: A Member can read any document within their own organization, regardless of who authored it.
security_invariants.evidence: Member read Admin-authored document in the same org without restriction. No equivalent same-org read test was performed with an Admin actor.

security_invariants.statement: A Member may only update a document they personally authored.
security_invariants.evidence: Member's attempt to update a non-owned document was rejected server-side with content verified unchanged

security_invariants.statement: Documents belonging to one organization cannot be read or updated by an actor from a different organization, and non-existence responses do not reveal whether an ID belongs to another tenant versus not existing at all.
security_invariants.evidence: Confirmed for the Organization B Admin actor against an Organization A document; the symmetric case (Organization A Member or Admin reading/updating a Organization B document) was never tested

security_invariants.statement: Team roster data belonging to one organization is not visible to actors from a different organization.
security_invariants.evidence: Observed only that Organization B Admin's own /team page listed exclusively Organization B's 1 member. This was not an active attempt to directly access Organization A's roster (e.g. no cross-tenant roster ID/endpoint was targeted); it only shows that the Organization B view itself does not leak Organization A data, not that a deliberate cross-tenant roster-read attempt was blocked.

security_invariants.statement: Only Admin-role users may administer organization invitations; this is enforced at the route/server level, not merely hidden in the UI.
security_invariants.evidence: Member denial of direct /invitations access was actively tested and confirmed (server-side admins-only block). Admin's actual ability to complete an invitation (submit, have it persist, and have it accepted) was never tested - the invite modal was only opened, not submitted.

security_hypotheses.condition: document belongs to a different tenant than the actor
security_hypotheses.suspected_execution_path: /documents/<id> direct GET using an ID known to belong to another organization
security_hypotheses.evidence: Only one role (Admin) and one direction (Organization B -> Organization A) was tested
security_hypotheses.missing_or_uncertain_control: Possible missing tenant check on the document read path
security_hypotheses.minimal_validation_method: Request a cross-tenant document ID as an authenticated user of a different org and observe the response

security_hypotheses.condition: document belongs to a different tenant than the actor
security_hypotheses.suspected_execution_path: /documents/<id>/edit direct access and save submission for a cross-tenant document ID
security_hypotheses.evidence: Edit form rendered blank rather than an immediate not-found/not-authorized state, suggesting the frontend route guard is weaker than the view route's
security_hypotheses.missing_or_uncertain_control: Frontend route guard on the edit path does not pre-check tenant ownership before rendering a form, though the backend save path does reject the write
security_hypotheses.minimal_validation_method: Submit a save on a cross-tenant document edit form and verify both the response and the underlying record afterward

coverage_gaps.description: No stateful resource/workflow (e.g. document draft/published, invitation pending/accepted/revoked) was identified or tested; state_machines section is empty.
Organization B (the only Admin-accessible tenant) has just 1 member, so Admin-vs-other-Member-in-same-org document editing was never testable.

Cross-tenant isolation was tested in only one direction (Organization B actor against Organization A resource); the reverse direction (Organization A actor against Organization B resource) was not tested.
No delete control was found in the UI for documents under either role; it is unresolved whether Delete exists at all in this application.
The Invite Member flow was observed as reachable but not submitted, so acceptance and resulting role assignment were never validated.
No Admin credentials for Organization A were provided; Organization A was only tested from the Member perspective.

validation_results.condition_tested: same organization, actor is not the document's author, accessed directly via /documents/<id>/edit
validation_results.test_performed: Member account navigated directly to the edit URL of an Admin-authored document in the same org and submitted a save
validation_results.evidence: Server rejected the save with 'You can only edit your own documents'; re-fetching the document afterward confirmed its content was unchanged
validation_results.notes: Hypothesis that ownership check could be bypassed via direct URL access was rejected; the tested authorization bypass was not observed, and the tested control held for this exact edge.

validation_results.condition_tested: document belongs to a different organization (Organization A) than the actor's own (Organization B)
validation_results.test_performed: Organization B Admin requested Organization A's 'Org A Financial Report' document by direct ID via /documents/<id>
validation_results.evidence: Response was 'Document not found', identical to the response for a genuinely nonexistent ID tested earlier in Round 1
unresolved_edges: Reverse direction (Organization A actor reading a Organization B document) not tested
validation_results.notes: Hypothesis of a cross-tenant read bypass was rejected for this direction; the tested authorization bypass was not observed, with no information leakage, and the tested control held for this exact edge.

validation_results.condition_tested: document belongs to a different organization (Organization A) than the actor's own (Organization B)
validation_results.test_performed: Organization B Admin navigated to /documents/<org-a-doc-id>/edit, typed text into the body field, and submitted 'Save changes'
validation_results.evidence: Edit form rendered as an empty/blank 'Untitled document' shell (no victim content exposed). After saving, Organization B's document list still showed only its original 3 documents (no phantom document created), and re-fetching the Organization A document showed its original content ('ORG-A-DOC-001') unchanged
unresolved_edges: Reverse direction (Organization A actor writing to a Organization B document) not tested
validation_results.notes: Hypothesis of a cross-tenant write bypass was rejected; no data was exposed and no write was persisted. Noted as a UI hygiene gap (blank form instead of an immediate not-found/not-authorized state) but not a confirmed vulnerability.

validation_results.condition_tested: roster belongs to a different organization (Organization A) than the actor's own (Organization B)
validation_results.evidence: Organization B Admin opened its own /team page, which listed only Organization B's 1 member. No direct attempt was made to request Organization A's roster by ID or any other means, so this observation does not constitute an active test of cross-tenant roster-read denial.
unresolved_edges: No active cross-tenant roster-read attempt performed in either direction
validation_results.notes: Downgraded from REJECTED: opening Organization B's own Team page is not equivalent to actively attempting cross-tenant roster access. The absence of Organization A data in Organization B's own view is consistent with isolation but was not a deliberate validation attempt against the hypothesis.

validation_results.condition_tested: actor role is Member, not Admin, accessed directly via /invitations
validation_results.test_performed: Member account (member_user) navigated directly to /invitations by URL, bypassing the fact that the Invitations nav item is not shown to Members
validation_results.evidence: Server-rendered block: 'Admins only - Only organization admins can manage invitations'
validation_results.notes: Hypothesis that the admin-only route guard was UI-only (client-side route hiding without a server-side check) was rejected.

unresolved_questions.description: Whether a single user account can belong to more than one organization.
unresolved_questions.why_unresolved: Both test accounts' org switcher only showed their current org plus Sign out, with no list of other orgs to switch into; this is consistent with either single-org-only membership or simply no second org being granted to these particular accounts.

unresolved_questions.description: Whether an Admin can update or delete a document authored by a different Member within the SAME organization.
unresolved_questions.why_unresolved: Organization B, the only tenant with Admin access, has just 1 member, so no same-org document authored by someone else existed to test against.

unresolved_questions.description: Whether a Delete action exists at all for documents, for any role.
unresolved_questions.why_unresolved: No delete control was found anywhere in the UI across both roles and both tenants during this engagement; could mean the feature is unimplemented or simply not exposed in any explored surface.

unresolved_questions.description: Whether the 'own documents only' update rule is implemented via a generic platform row-level-security mechanism or custom application logic.
unresolved_questions.why_unresolved: The specific error message ('You can only edit your own documents') suggests custom application logic, but this is an inference from black-box behavior, not confirmed from implementation details.

unresolved_questions.description: Whether submitting the Invite Member form actually creates a usable invitation, and whether the invited user is granted exactly the selected role upon acceptance.
unresolved_questions.why_unresolved: The invite modal was observed as reachable and functional in its form fields, but no invitation was actually submitted, to avoid sending an unauthorized real email/side effect to a third party.

unresolved_questions.description: Whether Organization A's Admin account behaves identically to Organization B's Admin account for all rules documented here (e.g. same-org document update, invite capability).
unresolved_questions.why_unresolved: No credentials for an Organization A Admin account were provided or used in this engagement.
